newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/3Com calls busy, stock off again. [corrected 21:15 gmt]
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/3Com calls busy, stock off again. [corrected 21:15 gmt]

text.p: Call options on 3Com Corp were heavily traded as the stock fell sharply for a second straight session.
Eight of the 10 most active calls at the Pacific Stock Exchange were 3Com calls but not one 3Com (corrects from Cisco Systems Inc) put made the most actives list.
"Everyone is playing one side. That's kind of scary," said one options strategist.
The stock was down 12-3/8 at 38-3/8 on volume of about 32 million shares by 1400 CST/2000 GMT.
It hit a session low of 37.
3Com stock closed down nearly two points last Friday after being down five intraday and was trading above 70 just a month ago.

The network equipment maker said Monday its fiscal third quarter earnings would fall short of Wall Street expectations and analysts said rising competition from Intel Corp could pressure earnings for more quarters.
"They said the nasty words," one options broker said.
Michael Schwartz, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said some of the 3Com call volume could be from investors rolling February positions out to March.
February options expire at the end of next week.
Schwartz added that investors rolling 3Com positions were "perennial optimists" paying a hefty price.
The 3Com February 45 calls were trading at 9/16, down 6-1/16 and the March 45 calls were trading at 1-5/8, down six.
"Even though you have limited risk in trading options, if you keep on losing a limited amount of money, you're going to get wiped out," Schwartz said.
The busiest 3Com option was the February 45 call, with volume of about 5,770 contracts. It had open interest of 984 contracts.
Other busy calls included the February 65 call with volume of nearly 4,400 and the February 50 call with volume of 4,170.
The March 45 and 50 calls and the April 25 calls also were busy.
On the put side, the most active option was the April 40, with volume of 650 contracts. It was up 3-1/2 at 4-3/4.
The options broker said some of the call volume was likely from investors exiting positions outright rather than rolling out into March or April.
The selloff in 3Com naturally drove volatilities sharply higher, with the February 35 calls breaking 90, traders said.

"It has pumped up there quite a bit," the options broker said. He said the volatility in the February 45 call, normally around 54, was around 70. The February 50 call volatility was about 88, the 40 call 85.
Volatilities in the March calls were mostly in the 60s.
The selloff spilled over into Cisco Systems, another network equipment company, which slid 4-5/8 to 58-1/8 in heavy afternoon trading.
Cisco calls were more active than puts, but several puts, including the February 55, 60 and 65, did see heavy volume.
((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
